pr_title: feat: add support for DISTINCT queries
pr_comments: There is no `join` option in `next` so I would like to ask you not to change that part. You'll be able to do distinct only using select query builder.

> There is no `join` option in `next`

Ah, a bit silly of me, but I didn't even think to look at the `next` branch.

It might be worth updating the [contributing doc](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) to mention PRs should be against `next` instead of `master`.

> You'll be able to do distinct only using select query builder.

Is there a issue/discussion around this I can refer to in order to get a grasp on the motivation for the change?

Based on the way TypeORM is _presently_ designed, being able to specify joins (and in particular relationship aliases) with the "entity manger" is critical functionality. Needing to fallback to the `QueryBuilder` would _significantly_ detract from the usefulness of TypeORM as an ORM.

Specifically because relations will be split across tables, we regularly need a way to perform queries based on these relations. The example in my post above is pretty straight-forward i.e. "We want all users with at least one post".

MongoDB has no problem performing these sorts of queries on relations because the relations can be e.g. profile pics can be embedded in users, so it'd be trivial to query users who have a profile pic. 

Without being able to reference relations (alias the join) in a `find()` operation then relational databases will be _significantly_ handicapped compared to what TypeORM offers document-oriented DBs (MongoDB).

If there's some alternative to the `join` syntax, then that's fine, but not being able to perform queries based on relations would be a deal breaker for us.

Haven't had a chance to try out `next`, but I see the change log mentions `QueryBuilder` will now load eager relationships - if that's the case, it might be enough to address my concerns.

I'll rebase this on `next` (minus the `JoinOptions` stuff) when I get a chance.

>> "We want all users with at least one post".

> how do you do it with find right now? In next where expressions automatically create inner joins, e.g.
> [...]
> `SELECT * FROM user INNER JOIN post WHERE post.id=1`

That's not the correct query, we're after:

> `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM user INNER JOIN post ON post.user_id=user.id`

The example code in my initial post is actually performing this same query, albeit in an overly verbose fashion i.e.

```typescript
const users = getRepository<User>(User).find({
	join: {
		alias: 'user',
		distinct: true,
		leftJoin: {
			post: 'user.posts',
		}
	},
	where: "user.id = post.user_id",
})
```

This outputs the query:

> SELECT DISTINCT \<USER FIELD SELECTIONS\> FROM "users" "user" LEFT JOIN "posts" "post" ON "post"."user_id"="user"."id" WHERE "user"."id" = post.user_id

`LEFT JOIN` is just used for illustration purposes; an `INNER JOIN` (`innerJoin` instead of `leftJoin`) would of course eliminate the need for the `WHERE` clause entirely.  


**Anyway...**

The changes you've already made to `QueryBuilder` on `next` (e.g. enabled eager loading), actually address my concerns with using it. Basically, I just didn't like the idea that using `QueryBuilder` would cause me to miss out on some ORM benefits. For example, in the future if I wanted to change a model to enable eager loading, I wouldn't then want to have to go update every single `QueryBuilder` query simply because it didn't support eager loading.

I'm actually very comfortable using `QueryBuilder`, it's a far superior API to `find()`. It _was_ just missing functionality (on `master`) that `find()` supported, and that concerned me.

Now that's no longer the case, I actually see very little reason for `find()` to exist at all; if it were deprecated I wouldn't miss it.
Any chance of merging this any time soon?
Any ETA for when this will be released? This is critical for us :)

Is there any way to SELECT DISTINCT using query builder?
comments: @dariusmb can you please tell us more about your problem?

I'm facing an issue with DISTINCT and Query Builder too, I don't know if it's the same that was reported here though, in my case if I do:
```
const applications = await Application.createQueryBuilder("applications")
    .select('DISTINCT ON (applications.id) applications.id', 'id')
    .addSelect('applications.loan_number', 'loanNumber')
    .addSelect('applicant.id', 'applicantId')
    .addSelect('ass.status', 'signature_status')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationApplicants', 'applicant')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationSignatureStatus', 'ass')
    .where("applications.deleted_at = null")
    .orderBy("applications.id", "DESC")
    .limit(4)
    .getRawMany();
```
The first select is not being placed as the first select, resulting in a syntax error:
```
SELECT 
"applicant"."id" AS "applicantId",
"ass"."status" AS "signature_status",
DISTINCT ON ("applications"."id") "applications"."id" AS "id",
applications.loan_number AS "loanNumber"
FROM "public"."applications" "applications"
LEFT JOIN "public"."application_applicants" "applicant" ON "applicant"."application_id"="applications"."id" 
ORDER BY "applications"."id" DESC
LIMIT 4
```
`error: { error: syntax error at or near "DISTINCT"`


**Database system/driver:**
[X ] postgres

**TypeORM version:**
[X] 0.2.7

Why not simply:

```
const applications = await Application.createQueryBuilder("applications")
    .select('DISTINCT applications.id', 'id')
    .addSelect('applications.loan_number', 'loanNumber')
    .addSelect('applicant.id', 'applicantId')
    .addSelect('ass.status', 'signature_status')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationApplicants', 'applicant')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationSignatureStatus', 'ass')
    .where("applications.deleted_at = null")
    .orderBy("applications.id", "DESC")
    .limit(4)
    .getRawMany();
```
?
@afurculita The Postgres `DISTINCT ON` behaves a bit different from `DISTINCT` clause, I simplified the query a bit just to post here, but anyway, the same problem happens with `DISTINCT`

Wouldn't be interesting if we had a `distinct` method ? Like in KNEX we have:
```
knex('tablename').distinct(knex.raw('ON (column) column'))
.orderBy('column')
.orderBy('another_column');
```
Same issue here, the `DISTINCT ON` select is not getting placed as the first select => syntax error
I made a PR fixing this issue https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/3065

@gabrielshawandpartners bit late to the party perhaps but i've found that writing this as one long select works (in the regular branch). may be helpful for people experiencing the same:
`const applications = await Application.createQueryBuilder("applications")
    .select('DISTINCT ON (applications.id) applications.id as id, applications.loan_number' as "loanNumber", applicant.id' as "applicantId", ass.status as "signature_status"')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationApplicants', 'applicant')
    .leftJoin('applications.applicationSignatureStatus', 'ass')
    .where("applications.deleted_at = null")
    .orderBy("applications.id", "DESC")
    .limit(4)
    .getRawMany();
`
(sorry for the formatting. just drop this ^ in your editor of choice i suppose :))

review_comments: In general we should try to not compare query text in our tests, but the behavior.  If for some reason we would change default naming strategy in the future we would have to modify many tests. However this(wrong) approach is used in this file, so I'm ok with it here.
